role: Compile and execute the application.
artifact_or_tool: JDK for development; compatible JVM runtime for distribution
version_policy: Recommend Java 21 LTS as a conservative baseline; pin a supported patch release and verify the selected dependencies.
rationale: Use a maintained JVM distribution for Kotlin and GreenMail.
integration_notes: Set the Kotlin JVM target and Gradle toolchain consistently; README still describes Swift so the language change remains a design decision.

role: Implement the CLI and fixture management layer.
version_policy: Pin one Kotlin release compatible with the selected Gradle and JVM versions; align compiler plugins and standard library.
rationale: Provide Kotlin development ergonomics while using GreenMail's Java interfaces directly.
integration_notes: Keep the project JVM-only initially; a separate native runtime is unnecessary for the stated scope.

role: Resolve dependencies and run compilation and verification.
version_policy: Pin the Wrapper distribution compatible with the Kotlin plugin and build JDK; record its checksum.
rationale: Give contributors and CI the same build tool without requiring a global Gradle installation.
integration_notes: Pin dependency versions and review the resolved graph; final compatibility requires a working build rather than independent version guesses.

role: Package the CLI with launcher scripts and runtime libraries.
artifact_or_tool: Gradle application plugin; installDist; distZip; distTar
version_policy: Use the version bundled with the pinned Gradle distribution.
rationale: Provide a small distribution workflow suitable for host execution and copying into a container.
integration_notes: Recommend a distribution with separate dependency JARs initially; verify launcher signal behavior and include a compatible JVM in the container.

role: Provide IMAP protocol handling and runtime mailbox storage.
version_policy: Evaluate the stable 2.1.x line; pin a released patch after lifecycle and compatibility checks.
rationale: Reuse IMAP and filesystem import rather than build a protocol server.
integration_notes: Embed the core library; greenmail-core is a repository module name. Enable only IMAP and verify account cleanup; folders; reset; flags; dates; and session invalidation.

role: Represent existing messages and access IMAP in integration tests.
version_policy: Align with the selected GreenMail release; use the jakarta.mail namespace for the proposed 2.1.x baseline.
rationale: Provide standard message and mailbox interfaces.
integration_notes: GreenMail brings the API transitively; declare it directly if application or test code imports its types. Avoid mixing javax.mail and jakarta.mail stacks.

role: Supply the Jakarta Mail implementation and an IMAP client for tests.
artifact_or_tool: org.eclipse.angus:jakarta.mail as declared by GreenMail; inspect the selected release graph
version_policy: Keep the provider compatible with GreenMail's Jakarta Mail API; avoid independent overrides initially.
rationale: Reuse the mail provider already required by GreenMail.
integration_notes: Exercise read; fetch; search; and mutation through a real IMAP client; no sending feature or SMTP listener is required. Verify MIME and charset fidelity.

role: Support MIME content and attachment handling.
version_policy: Use versions resolved by the selected GreenMail release unless a verified alignment change is needed.
rationale: Provide MIME activation support in the existing mail stack.
integration_notes: Inspect the resolved runtime distribution to ensure the API and provider are packaged; no separate attachment framework is initially proposed.

role: Parse commands; selectors; options; and generate help.
version_policy: Pin a release compatible with the Kotlin/JVM baseline.
rationale: Provide a Kotlin command framework for the proposed grouped CLI.
integration_notes: Recommend the core artifact for simple script-friendly output; choose the Mordant-enabled variant only if richer terminal presentation is useful. Implement stable result and exit behavior in the application.

role: Read fixture metadata and produce machine-readable CLI results.
version_policy: Pin a runtime release compatible with the selected Kotlin compiler; runtime and compiler plugin version numbers need not match.
rationale: Use one Kotlin JSON library for the small metadata and result models.
integration_notes: Schema conventions remain open; parsing must be complemented by fixture validation and explicit unknown-field policy. Keep .eml bytes outside JSON serialization. Reuse this JSON library for the small supported Toxiproxy API subset if enabled.

role: Generate serializers for declared Kotlin metadata and result types.
version_policy: Use the same version as the Kotlin JVM compiler plugin.
rationale: Support typed JSON models without hand-writing serialization code.
integration_notes: Required when using generated serializers for application types; pure JSON-tree parsing can avoid this plugin if typed models are not adopted.

role: Discover and read fixture trees with explicit path boundaries.
version_policy: Use the selected JVM's bundled implementation.
rationale: Cover path resolution; file reads; directory traversal; and filesystem metadata without another file utility library.
integration_notes: The application still defines stable sorting; selector boundaries; symlink policy; and source immutability. Filesystem APIs do not supply fixture semantics.

role: Coordinate management operations and graceful shutdown.
version_policy: Use the selected JVM's bundled implementation.
rationale: Support serialization of state-changing operations with a small runtime dependency surface.
integration_notes: Start with straightforward coordination suitable for GreenMail's blocking interfaces; coroutines are optional if later needs justify them. No transactional mailbox isolation is implied.

role: Accept local CLI control requests in the running server process.
version_policy: Use the selected JVM module; include it in any reduced runtime image.
rationale: A candidate for a small local HTTP control mechanism without an application web framework.
integration_notes: Use only if local HTTP is selected; bind management separately from IMAP and define instance discovery and access protection. A local socket choice would replace this row.

role: Send CLI management requests when local HTTP is selected; also control the optional Toxiproxy daemon.
version_policy: Use the same JVM baseline as the CLI; retain this module in any reduced runtime image.
rationale: Pair the built-in client with a small local HTTP management endpoint.
integration_notes: Conditional on HTTP control; define request timeouts and unavailable-instance errors. Keep management traffic local by default and separate from IMAP client traffic. The Toxiproxy adapter needs HTTP independently of the application control-transport choice; reuse this JDK client and the existing JSON library when the extension is enabled.

role: Log application lifecycle and library diagnostics.
version_policy: Match the API generation used by the selected GreenMail release.
rationale: Use the logging facade already employed by GreenMail.
integration_notes: Declare directly if application code imports it; choose exactly one compatible runtime logging provider and avoid routing loops.

role: Configure log levels and direct diagnostic logs to stderr.
version_policy: Pin a supported version compatible with the resolved SLF4J API and JVM.
rationale: Offer one configurable provider for application and GreenMail diagnostics.
integration_notes: Configure stderr explicitly so JSON stdout remains clean; avoid logging credentials or message contents by default. A simpler SLF4J provider is an alternative if configuration needs remain minimal.

role: Run fixture validation; lifecycle; CLI; and IMAP integration tests.
version_policy: Pin a compatible JUnit release using its BOM; configure Gradle useJUnitPlatform and verify compatibility with Kotlin test tooling.
rationale: Provide assertions; parameterized tests; temporary directories; and a standard JVM test runner.
integration_notes: Test management behavior and connect through IMAP for protocol-visible outcomes; launch the actual application for cross-process CLI checks. JUnit dependencies belong in test configurations.

role: Optionally manage isolated GreenMail instances in adapter tests.
version_policy: Match the GreenMail Core version and verify compatibility with the chosen JUnit generation.
rationale: Provide a convenience lifecycle helper for narrowly scoped GreenMail integration tests.
integration_notes: Do not require this helper for production startup or tests of the application's own lifecycle; explicit setup and cleanup may be sufficient.

role: Build and run the fixture-driven application image.
artifact_or_tool: docker build; docker run; docker exec; docker stop
version_policy: Document and test a supported engine baseline; contributors may use Podman instead.
rationale: Support familiar image builds; read-only bind mounts; published ports; and in-container CLI management.
integration_notes: Not an application JVM dependency; use a custom image containing the management application rather than assuming stock GreenMail implements the proposed CLI.

role: Provide an alternative container build and execution workflow.
artifact_or_tool: podman build; podman run; podman exec; podman stop
version_policy: Document and test a supported Podman baseline with the same application image.
rationale: Support developers who use Podman rather than Docker.
integration_notes: Users need one engine rather than both; verify mount permissions; rootless execution; port publishing; and signal-driven shutdown on supported platforms.

role: Supply the container build JDK and runtime JVM.
artifact_or_tool: eclipse-temurin image family; explicit JDK builder and runtime tags
version_policy: Match the selected Java major version; pin image digests at release and deliberately refresh them.
rationale: Use the same JVM family across host verification and container execution.
integration_notes: Select published tags and required architectures during packaging; run the application as non-root and include filesystem and any chosen management modules.

role: Assemble the CSV design inputs and generate deterministic documentation.
version_policy: Pin the repository-supported CLI version when the app.cue documentation model is introduced.
rationale: Continue the established design-meta workflow with reusable CSV source artifacts.
integration_notes: Used only for design documentation; not required to run the IMAP server. These CSV files remain design inputs until registered in a flyb configuration.

role: Proxy TCP connections between IMAP clients and GreenMail.
artifact_or_tool: toxiproxy-server; separately managed host binary or container
version_policy: Pin a released Toxiproxy version and verify latency; jitter; timeout; reset_peer; bandwidth; and proxy enable/disable behavior on supported platforms.
rationale: Provide opt-in network impairment without changing the IMAP protocol implementation.
integration_notes: Not embedded in the JVM and not needed for default startup or tests. Use the JDK HTTP client and existing JSON library for a narrow adapter; no extra Java Toxiproxy SDK or Go toolchain is initially required.

role: Run the optional daemon on a private container network.
version_policy: Use an explicit release tag and pinned digest matching the verified server version; check supported architectures.
rationale: Separate the optional proxy lifecycle from the default mail-server image.
integration_notes: Publish only the intended client-facing IMAP listener for proxied tests; keep API and backend internal. Support the same companion topology with Docker and Podman; normal forwarding still carries proxy overhead and failure risk.
